name: Ubayy bin Kab
title: Master of the Reciters (Sayyid al-Qurra') & Syrian Codex
biography: A senior Medinan Companion from the Ansar whom Prophet Muhammad declared the greatest reciter of the Quran in the community ('aqra'ukum Ubayy') and to whom the Prophet personally recited by divine command (Sahih al-Bukhari 4959). Ubayy served as the Prophet's chief Medinan scribe and compiled a renowned personal Mushaf that circulated widely in Syria prior to the Uthmanic standardization. Classical sources (including Sahih Muslim 1050, Tafsir al-Tabari, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir) record that Ubayy's codex included two additional short supplicatory chapters (Surat al-Khal' and Surat al-Hafd), preserved the Valley of Gold passage, and contained numerous explicit legal and exegetical clauses such as 'to an appointed time' in 4:24 and 'and he is a father to them' in 33:6.

virtues.hadith_arabic: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لأُبَىٍّ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَمَرَنِي أَنْ أَقْرَأَ عَلَيْكَ ‏{‏لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ وَسَمَّانِي قَالَ: نَعَمْ. فَبَكَى
virtues.hadith_english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Ubayy: "Allah has ordered me to recite to you: 'Those who disbelieve from among the People of the Scripture' (Surah 98)." Ubayy asked: "Did He mention me by name to you?" The Prophet answered: "Yes." Whereupon Ubayy wept.

virtues.hadith_arabic: قَالَ عُمَرُ أُبَىٌّ أَقْرَؤُنَا وَإِنَّا لَنَدَعُ مِنْ لَحَنِ أُبَىٍّ، وَأُبَىٌّ يَقُولُ أَخَذْتُهُ مِنْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلاَ أَتْرُكُهُ لِشَىْءٍ
virtues.hadith_english: Umar said: "Ubayy is the best of us in the recitation (of the Qur'an), yet we leave some of what Ubayy recites." Ubayy says: "I have taken it directly from the mouth of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), so I will not leave it for anything whatsoever."

variants.short_title: 'One Community, Then They Differed' in 2:213
variants.plain_english_hook: Surah 2:213 jumps directly from 'The people were one community' to 'Then God raised up the prophets'; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices supplied the missing link: 'then they differed'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:213 — Addition of 'Fa-Ikhtalafu' in Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:213, the verse begins 'The people were (once) one community. Then God raised up the prophets as bringers of good news and warners' (كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ), leaving unstated why prophets were sent if humanity was united. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via authentic chains from Ibn Abbas and Abu al-'Aliyah that the recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b explicitly included 'then they differed' (كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَاخْتَلَفُوا فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ), and also note that Ubayy read 'and so that they may be witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection' near the end of the verse.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars explain that the Uthmanic text relies on rhetorical ellipsis (idmar) where 'then they differed' is understood from the later phrase 'to judge among the people concerning their differences', while treating the Companion wording as an explanatory gloss.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite the authenticated report of Ibn Abbas (graded sahih by al-Hakim) appealing directly to the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b ('fa-ikhtalafu') to supply the verb required by the narrative logic of the verse.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 4048 - حدثنا محمد بن بشار، قال: حدثنا أبو داود، قال: حدثنا همام بن منبه، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان بين نوح وآدم عشرة قرون، كلهم على شريعة من الحق، فاختلفوا، فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين، قال: وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ". وهي في قراءة أبي بن كعب: ( وليكونوا شهداء على الناس ) يوم القيامة ( والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 4048 - Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us... from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Between Nuh and Adam were ten generations, all of them upon a law of truth, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners. He said: And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The people were one community, then they differed." And it is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: {(And so that they would be witnesses over the people)} on the Day of Resurrection {(And God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path)}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The people were one community, then they differed."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : كان بين نوح وآدم عشرة قرون ، كلهم على شريعة من الحق . فاختلفوا ، فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين . قال : وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا " . ورواه الحاكم في مستدركه ، من حديث بندار عن محمد بن بشار . ثم قال : صحيح ولم يخرجاه . وكذا روى أبو جعفر الرازي ، عن أبي العالية ، عن أبي بن كعب : أنه كان يقرؤها : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: From 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Between Nuh and Adam were ten generations, all of them upon a law of truth. Then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners." He said: "And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'The people were one community, then they differed.'" Al-Hakim recorded it in his Mustadrak... and said: "It is Sahih, though they (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Similarly, Abu Ja'far Ar-Razi narrated from Abu Al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy bin Ka'b, that he used to recite it: "The people were one community, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners."

variants.short_title: 2:229 — 'Unless They Think' vs. 'Unless They Fear'
variants.plain_english_hook: In the divorce law of 2:229, an ancient Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b replaced 'unless the two of them fear... But if you fear' with 'unless the two of them think... But if the two of them think.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Think' (Yaẓunnā / Ẓannā) for 'Fear' in Ubayy's Mushaf on 2:229
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 2:229, the Uthmanic text governs khul' divorce with the clauses 'إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِۖ فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ' ('unless the two of them fear that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God. But if you fear that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God'). Al-Tabari (3797) records that Maymun bin Mihran and Ayyub inspected an ancient Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b and found it written: 'إِلَّا أَنْ يَظُنَّا أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَإِنْ ظَنَّا أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ' ('unless the two of them think... But if the two of them think'), while Ibn Mas'ud read 'إِلَّا أَنْ تَخَافُوا' ('unless you [plural] fear').

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari argues that classical Arabic poetry occasionally uses 'fear' (khawf) and 'presumption/thought' (ẓann) interchangeably when referring to anticipated future outcomes.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tabari 3797, Maymun bin Mihran and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani report physically examining an ancient, reliably transmitted Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b that both replaced the verb root (kh-w-f to ẓ-n-n) and kept the second verb in the dual ('if the two of them think') rather than switching to the second-person plural ('if you fear').

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد ذكر أن ذلك في قراءة أبي بن كعب : " إلا أن يظنا ألا يقيما حدود الله " . 3797 - حدثنا الحسن بن يحيى , قال : أخبرنا عبد الرزاق , قال : أخبرنا معمر , قال : أخبرني ثور , عن ميمون بن مهران , قال : في حرف أبي بن كعب إن الفداء تطليقة . قال : فذكرت ذلك لأيوب , فأتينا رجلا عنده مصحف قديم لأبي خرج من ثقة , فقرأناه فإذا فيه : " إلا أن يظنا ألا يقيما حدود الله , فإن ظنا ألا يقيما حدود الله فلا جناح عليهما فيما افتدت به " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It has been mentioned that this is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "unless they both presume that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God". 3797 — Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, he said: Thawr informed me, from Maymun bin Mihran, who said: In the mode of Ubayy bin Ka'b, the ransom is one pronouncement of divorce. variants.short_title: Who Knows the Ambiguous Verses in 3:7?
variants.plain_english_hook: Scholars debated for centuries where the sentence breaks in 3:7; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices worded the clause so that only God knows the ambiguous verses' interpretation.
variants.title: Surah Al 'Imran 3:7 — Syntactic Separation of 'Those Firm in Knowledge'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 3:7 (وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ), exegetes and theologians were divided over whether 'and those firmly grounded in knowledge' is conjoined to 'God' (meaning scholars also know the interpretation of ambiguous verses) or begins a new sentence. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud's reading was 'Its interpretation is only with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say, We believe in it' (إِنْ تَأْوِيلُهُ إِلَّا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ), while Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'and those firmly grounded in knowledge say' (وَيَقُولُ الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ), both syntactically precluding conjunction with God.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: No one knows its interpretation except God.
variants.variant_target_english: Its interpretation is only with God.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَٰتٞ مُّحۡكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتٞۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ زَيۡغٞ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦۖ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ تَأۡوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱلرَّـٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلّٞ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَاۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: He (it is) who has sent down on you the Book, of which some verses are clearly composed – they are the mother of the Book – but others are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts (there is) a turning aside, they follow the ambiguous part of it, seeking (to cause) trouble and seeking its interpretation. No one knows its interpretation except God. And (as for) the ones firmly grounded in knowledge, they say, ‘We believe in it. All (of it) is from our Lord.’ Yet no one takes heed except those with understanding.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators cite the readings of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b as explanatory recitations (qira'at tafsiriyya) proving that a mandatory pause (waqf) falls after the name of God in the Uthmanic text.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explicitly rely on the non-Uthmanic wording of Ibn Mas'ud ('in ta'wiluhu illa 'inda Allah') and Ubayy bin Ka'b ('wa yaqulu al-rasikhuna') to settle a foundational theological dispute over whether human scholars can know the ta'wil of the mutashabihat.

variants.short_title: 3:81 — Covenant of the Book's People vs. Prophets
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says God took a covenant with 'the prophets,' Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'those who were given the Book,' with Mujahid calling 'prophets' a scribal error.
variants.title: Substitution of 'Those Given the Book' for 'The Prophets' in 3:81
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 3:81, the Uthmanic text reads 'وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ' ('when God took a covenant with the prophets'). Al-Tabari records via two authentic chains from Mujahid (7323–7324) and from al-Rabi' bin Anas (7325) that in the recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b it read 'وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ' ('when God took a covenant with those who were given the Book').
variants.variant_target_english: a covenant with those who were given the Book
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكُم مِّن كِتَٰبٖ وَحِكۡمَةٖ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولٞ مُّصَدِّقٞ لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ لَتُؤۡمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥۚ قَالَ ءَأَقۡرَرۡتُمۡ وَأَخَذۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمۡ إِصۡرِيۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَقۡرَرۡنَاۚ قَالَ فَٱشۡهَدُواْ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: (Remember) when God took a covenant with the prophets: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom, when a messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you are to believe in him and you are to help him.’ He said, ‘Do you agree and accept My burden on that (condition)?’ They said, ‘We agree.’ He said, ‘Bear witness, and I shall be with you among the witnesses.’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari argues that single-chain reports attributing variant readings or scribal errors to Companions cannot override the consensus codex, and later editors suggest Mujahid only meant the scribe wrote an earlier recitation instead of the final review.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tabari 7323–7324, Mujahid explicitly states regarding 'covenant with the prophets': 'It is an error from the scribe (هي خطأ من الكاتب), and in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is: And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book.'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 7323 - حدثني محمد بن عمرو قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم، عن عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد في قوله: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة "، قال: هي خطأ من الكاتب، وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ". (37) 7325 - حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا إسحاق قال، حدثنا عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع في قوله: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين "، يقول: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب، وكذلك كان يقرؤها الربيع: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب "، إنما هي أهل الكتاب. قال: وكذلك كان يقرأها أبي بن كعب.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: **7323** - *Muhammad bin ‘Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, from ‘Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying:* "(Remember) when God took a covenant with the prophets: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom’", he said: It is an error from the scribe, and it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas‘ud: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book." 7325 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah bin Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets", he says: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book," and thus Al-Rabi' used to recite it. He said: And thus Ubayy bin Ka'b used to recite it as well.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هي خطأ من الكاتب، وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is an error from the scribe, and it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas‘ud: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book."

variants.variant_arabic: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكُم مِّن كِتَٰبٖ وَحِكۡمَةٖ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولٞ مُّصَدِّقٞ لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ لَتُؤۡمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥۚ قَالَ ءَأَقۡرَرۡتُمۡ وَأَخَذۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمۡ إِصۡرِيۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَقۡرَرۡنَاۚ قَالَ فَٱشۡهَدُواْ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ
variants.variant_english: (Remember) when God took a covenant with those who were given the Book: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom, when a messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you are to believe in him and you are to help him.’ He said, ‘Do you agree and accept My burden on that (condition)?’ They said, ‘We agree.’ He said, ‘Bear witness, and I shall be with you among the witnesses.’
variants.hadith_arabic: 7323 - حدثني محمد بن عمرو قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم، عن عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد في قوله: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة "، قال: هي خطأ من الكاتب، وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ". (37) 7325 - حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا إسحاق قال، حدثنا عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع في قوله: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين "، يقول: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب، وكذلك كان يقرؤها الربيع: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب "، إنما هي أهل الكتاب. قال: وكذلك كان يقرأها أبي بن كعب.
variants.hadith_english: **7323** - *Muhammad bin ‘Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, from ‘Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying:* "(Remember) when God took a covenant with the prophets: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom’", he said: It is an error from the scribe, and it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas‘ud: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book." 7325 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah bin Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets", he says: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book," and thus Al-Rabi' used to recite it. He said: And thus Ubayy bin Ka'b used to recite it as well.

variants.short_title: 4:24 — 'For a Specified Term' in Marriage
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says 'what you enjoy from them, give them their marriage gifts,' Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Abbas read 'what you enjoy from them for a specified term.'
variants.title: Addition of 'For a Specified Term' (Ilā Ajalin Musammā) in 4:24
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 4:24, the Uthmanic text reads 'فَمَا ٱسۡتَمۡتَعۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡهُنَّ' ('So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple authentic chains that the codex of Ubayy bin Ka'b and the recitation of Ibn Abbas added the legal stipulation 'إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى' ('for a specified term'), with Ibn Abbas swearing three times that God revealed the verse with this phrase.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way
variants.variant_target_arabic: فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى
variants.variant_target_english: So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way for a specified term
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: ۞وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۖ كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَأُحِلَّ لَكُم مَّا وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُم مُّحۡصِنِينَ غَيۡرَ مُسَٰفِحِينَۚ فَمَا ٱسۡتَمۡتَعۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡهُنَّ فَـَٔاتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةٗۚ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِيمَا تَرَٰضَيۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡفَرِيضَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own. (This is) a written decree of God for you. (All women) beyond that are permitted to you to seek (to obtain) by means of your wealth, taking (them) in marriage, not in immorality. So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation. (There is) no blame on you in anything you may give them by mutual agreement beyond this obligation. Surely God is knowing, wise.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Sunni commentators argue that the phrase 'for a specified term' was either an explanatory gloss (qirā'a tafsīriyya) referring to early temporary marriage (mut'ah) or a wording whose recitation and legal ruling were subsequently abrogated.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tafsir al-Tabari (7181–7182), witnesses testify to physically inspecting the written Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b containing the phrase, and when Abu Nadrah objected that he did not read it that way, Ibn Abbas swore by God three times that God revealed it thus.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 7181 - حدثنا أبو كريب , قال : ثنا يحيى بن عيسى , قال : ثنا نصير بن أبي الأشعث , قال : ثني حبيب بن أبي ثابت , عن أبيه , قال : أعطاني ابن عباس مصحفا , فقال : هذا على قراءة أبي . قال أبو كريب , قال يحيى : فرأيت المصحف عند نصير فيه : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى " . 7184 - حدثنا ابن بشار , قال : ثنا عبد الأعلى , قال : ثنا سعيد , عن قتادة , قال : في قراءة أبي بن كعب : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 7181 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Yahya bin 'Isa narrated to us, he said: Nusayr bin Abi Al-Ash'ath narrated to us, he said: Habib bin Abi Thabit narrated to me, from his father, he said: Ibn 'Abbas gave me a Mus-haf and said: This is according to the recitation of Ubayy. Abu Kurayb said, Yahya said: So I saw the Mus-haf with Nusayr, and in it was: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them to a specified term." 7184 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said: In the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them to a specified term."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: فرأيت المصحف عند نصير فيه : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: So I saw the Mus-haf with Nusayr, and in it was: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them to a specified term."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد روي عن ابن عباس وطائفة من الصحابة القول بإباحتها للضرورة ، وهو رواية عن الإمام أحمد بن حنبل ، رحمهم الله تعالى . وكان ابن عباس ، وأبي بن كعب ، وسعيد بن جبير ، والسدي يقرءون : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة " . وقال مجاهد : نزلت في نكاح المتعة ، ولكن الجمهور على خلاف ذلك ، والعمدة ما ثبت في الصحيحين ، عن أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب [ رضي الله عنه ] قال : نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن نكاح المتعة وعن لحوم الحمر الأهلية يوم خيبر ولهذا الحديث ألفاظ مقررة هي في كتاب " الأحكام " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and a group of the Companions the view that it was permitted out of necessity, and it is a narration from Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on them). Ibn 'Abbas, Ubayy bin Ka'b, Sa'id bin Jubayr, and As-Suddi used to recite: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them *until a specified time*, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation." Mujahid stated that it was revealed about the Mut'ah marriage. But the majority are against that.

variants.short_title: 'Before Their Death' vs 'Before His Death' in 4:159
variants.plain_english_hook: Does 4:159 mean every Jew and Christian will believe in Jesus before 'his' (that person's or Jesus's) death? Ubayy bin Kab's reading had the plural 'before their death'.
variants.title: Surah An-Nisa 4:159 — 'Qabla Mawtihim' (Before Their Death) in Ubayy's Reading
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 4:159 (وَإِنْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ), the singular pronoun in 'before his death' (قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ) generated a major exegetical split over whether the pronoun refers to Jesus (after his eschatological descent) or to every individual among the People of the Book at the moment of dying. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple authentic chains (graded sahih by Ibn Kathir) that Ibn Abbas argued for the latter by citing the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: 'before their death' (قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِمْ).
variants.variant_target_english: before their death
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَإِن مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ إِلَّا لَيُؤۡمِنَنَّ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ مَوۡتِهِۦۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ يَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ شَهِيدٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Yet (there is) not one of the People of the Book except that he will indeed believe in it before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَإِن مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ إِلَّا لَيُؤۡمِنَنَّ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ مَوۡتِهِمۡۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ يَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ شَهِيدٗا
variants.variant_full_english: Yet (there is) not one of the People of the Book except that he will indeed believe in it before their death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir prefer interpreting the Uthmanic singular pronoun 'before his death' as referring to Jesus's future death after his second coming, treating Ubayy's plural 'before their death' as reflecting the alternative interpretation.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Ibn Kathir explicitly certifies that the chains to Ibn Abbas citing Ubayy bin Ka'b's reading 'qabla mawtihim' (with a final mim) are authentic (asanid sahiha), demonstrating how a single consonantal pronoun difference changes the verse from an eschatological prophecy about Jesus's return to a claim about every dying scripturalist.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 10814- حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال، حدثنا عبد الرحمن قال، حدثنا سفيان، عن أبي حصين، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: " وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته "، قال: في قراءة أبيّ: ( قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِمْ ). 10814م- حدثني إسحاق بن إبراهيم بن حبيب بن الشهيد قال، حدثنا عتاب بن بشير، عن خصيف، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: " وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته "، قال: هي في قراءة أبي: ( قبل موتهم ) ، ليس يهودي يموت أبدا حتى يؤمن بعيسى.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 10814m - Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin al-Shahid narrated to me... from Sa'id bin Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: {Yet (there is) not one of the People of the Book except that he will indeed believe in it before his death.} He said: "It is in the recitation of Ubayy: (before their death), no Jew ever dies until he believes in 'Isa."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هي في قراءة أبي: ( قبل موتهم )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is in the recitation of Ubayy: (before their death)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا عتاب بن بشير عن خصيف ، عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس : ( وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ) قال : هي في قراءة أبي : ( قبل موتهم ) ليس يهودي يموت أبدا حتى يؤمن بعيسى ... فهذه كلها أسانيد صحيحة إلى ابن عباس ، وكذا صح عن مجاهد ، وعكرمة ، ومحمد بن سيرين . وبه يقول الضحاك وجويبر ، والسدي ، وحكاه عن ابن عباس ، ونقل قراءة أبي بن كعب : " قبل موتهم " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: From Sa'id bin Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: > **{Yet (there is) not one of the People of the Book except that he will indeed believe in him before his death}** He said, "It is in the recitation of Ubayy: '(before their deaths).' No Jew ever dies until he believes in 'Isa."... All of these are authentic chains of narration to Ibn 'Abbas, and this is also authentic from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Muhammad bin Sirin. This is also the view of Ad-Dahhak, Juwaybir, and As-Suddi, who also related it from Ibn 'Abbas and mentioned the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "before their deaths."

tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is in the recitation of Ubayy: '(before their deaths).'

variants.short_title: Oath Atonement: 'Three Consecutive Days'
variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran requires fasting 'three days' to break an oath, leaving jurists divided on whether they must be back-to-back; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices explicitly added 'consecutive'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:89 — Addition of 'Mutatabi'at' (Consecutive) in Oath Expiation
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 5:89, the expiation for a broken oath when unable to feed or clothe the poor is 'a fast for three days' (فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple authentic chains that the codices and recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'a fast for three consecutive days' (فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ مُتَتَابِعَاتٍ), a variant that directly shaped Hanafi and Hanbali law requiring uninterrupted fasting.
variants.variant_target_english: a fast for three consecutive days

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 9750 - حدثنا عبد الأعلى بن واصل الأسدي، قال: ثنا عبيد الله بن موسى، عن أبي جعفر الرازي، عن الربيع بن أنس، عن أبي العالية، عن أبي بن كعب، أنه كان يقرأ: "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات". 9751 - حدثنا ابن وكيع، قال: ثنا يزيد بن هارون، عن قزعة بن سويد، عن سيف بن سليمان، عن مجاهد، قال: في قراءة عبد الله: "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات". فأما ما روي عن أبي وابن مسعود من قراءتهما "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات" فذلك خلاف ما في مصاحفنا، وغير جائز لنا أن نشهد بشيء ليس في مصاحفنا من الكلام أنه من كتاب الله.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 9750 - 'Abd al-A'la b. Wasil al-Asadi narrated to us... from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy b. Ka'b, that he used to read: 'a fast for three consecutive days'. 9751 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us... from Mujahid, he said: In the reading of 'Abd Allah: 'a fast for three consecutive days'. As for what was narrated from Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud regarding their reading 'a fast for three consecutive days', that is contrary to what is in our manuscripts of the Qur'an.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال أبو جعفر الرازي ، عن الربيع ، عن أبي العالية ، عن أبي بن كعب أنه كان يقرؤها : " فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات " . وحكاها مجاهد والشعبي وأبو إسحاق ، عن عبد الله بن مسعود . وقال إبراهيم : في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات " . وقال الأعمش : كان أصحاب ابن مسعود يقرءونها كذلك .

Al-A'mash said: 'The companions of Ibn Mas'ud used to read it like that.'

variants.short_title: 'He Has Studied' (Darasa) vs 'You Have Studied' (6:105)
variants.plain_english_hook: In 6:105, the standard Quran has 'so that they will say, You have studied' (darasta, with a final t); the codices of Ubayy and Ibn Masud read 'He has studied' (darasa).
variants.title: Surah Al-An'am 6:105 — 'Wa-li-Yaqulu Darasa' in Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud's Codices
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 6:105, the consonantal rasm دَرَسْتَ (with a final ta') is read by the majority as 'You have studied' (darasta), by Ibn Kathir/Abu 'Amr as 'You have studied with others' (darasta, adding an alif), and by Ibn 'Amir as 'They have become old/erased' (darasat). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim bin Sallam and Ma'mar from Qatadah that in the codex/harf of Ubayy bin Ka'b and Abdullah bin Mas'ud the word was written without the final ta': 'so that they will say, He has studied' (وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرَسَ).

variants.variant_target_english: so that they will say, ‘He has studied,’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari remarks that third-person 'darasa' and second-person 'darasta' both convey the disbelievers' allegation that the Prophet studied previous texts, while preferring 'darasta' because it conforms to the Uthmanic consonantal script.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The absence of the final consonant ta' in 'darasa' is attested by both Qatadah and Abu 'Ubayd for the codices (harf) of both Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b, representing a genuine consonantal divergence from the Uthmanic rasm.

variants.short_title: 7:127 — 'When They Have Forsaken You Not to Serve You'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where Pharaoh's chiefs ask if he will leave Moses 'to forsake you and your gods,' Ubayy bin Ka'b's codex read 'when they have forsaken you so as not to serve you and your gods.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'When They Have Forsaken You Not to Worship You' in 7:127
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 7:127, the Uthmanic text quotes Pharaoh's chiefs asking: 'أَتَذَرُ مُوسَىٰ وَقَوۡمَهُۥ لِيُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَيَذَرَكَ وَءَالِهَتَكَۚ' ('Will you leave Moses and his people to foment corruption on the earth and to forsake you and your gods?'). Both al-Tabari (14961) and Ibn Kathir record via Harun bin Musa that in the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy bin Ka'b this clause read 'وَقَدْ تَرَكُوكَ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوكَ وَآلِهَتَكَ' ('when they have forsaken you so as not to serve you and your gods').

variants.short_title: 'Almost Removed Mountains' (Kada vs Kana) in 14:46
variants.plain_english_hook: Whether 14:46 means their plot 'could never' move mountains or 'almost' moved mountains depends on one letter: standard 'kana' (was) vs Ibn Masud, Ubayy, Umar, and Ali's 'kada' (almost).
variants.title: Surah Ibrahim 14:46 — 'Wa-In Kada Makruhum' in Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy's Codices
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 14:46, the clause وَإِنْ كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبَالُ (with nun in 'kana') is interpreted by the majority of reciters (who read 'litazula') as a negation: 'and their scheme was not such as to remove the mountains.' Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud (in his Mushaf), Ubayy bin Ka'b, Umar bin al-Khattab, and Ali bin Abi Talib read وَإِنْ كَادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الْجِبَالُ (with dal in 'kada' and dammah on 'latazulu'), reversing the sense to an affirmative near-occurrence: 'and indeed their scheme almost removed the mountains by it.'

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari acknowledges that Companions and Successors recited 'wa-in kada' with a dal, but rules that it is impermissible to recite it today because the Uthmanic manuscripts are written 'wa-in kana' with a nun, and one may not alter the orthography of the Muslims' Mushafs.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari's explicit concession—that the Companion reading 'wa-in kada' (attested for Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf, Umar, Ali, and Ubayy) is grammatically sound and was adapted by the canonical Kufan reciter al-Kisa'i onto the Uthmanic rasm 'wa-in kana latazulu'—demonstrates how a non-Uthmanic consonantal variant directly generated a canonical Qira'at dispute.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال ابن جريج: أخبرني عمرو بن دينار ، عن عكرمة ، عن عمر بن الخطاب ، أنه كان يقرأ " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ ". قال قتادة: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ ". وذلك أن الذين قرءوا ذلك بفتح اللام الأولى ورفع الثانية قرءوا: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ " بالدال ، وهي إذا قرئت كذلك ، فالصحيح من القراءة مع " وَإِنْ كادَ " فتح اللام الأولى ورفع الثانية على ما قرءوا ، وغير جائز عندنا القراءة كذلك ، لأن مصاحفنا بخلاف ذلك ، وإنما خطَّ مصاحفنا وإن كان بالنون لا بالدال.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Amr bin Dinar informed me, from 'Ikrimah, from 'Umar bin al-Khattab, that he used to recite: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'. Qatadah said: And in the codex (Mushaf) of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'. And that is because those who recited it with a fathah on the first lam and a dammah on the second recited: '{wa-in kada makruhum}' with a dal... And it is not permissible in our view to recite like that, because our manuscripts are contrary to that. The script of our manuscripts is 'wa-in kana' with a nun, not with a dal.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the codex (Mushaf) of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال : فهو قول الله - عز وجل - : " وإن كاد مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال " . قال أبو إسحاق : وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله : " وإن كاد مكرهم " . قلت : وكذا روي عن أبي بن كعب ، وعمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنهما - أنهما قرآ : " وإن كاد " كما قرأ علي .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: This is the saying of Allah (the Exalted and Most Honored): 'though their plot was almost (*Wa in kad*) one to remove the mountains from their places.' variants.short_title: 17:23 — 'Your Lord Enjoined' vs. 'Your Lord Decreed'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran reads 'Your Lord has decreed (wa-qaḍā) that you worship none but Him,' Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy's codices read 'Your Lord has enjoined (wa-waṣṣā).'

variants.short_title: Ubayy's Codex Adds 'Every Sound Ship' in Q. 18:79
variants.plain_english_hook: In Ubayy bin Ka'b's codex—as well as Ibn Mas'ud's—verse 18:79 explicitly specifies that the king seized 'every sound ship' by force, supplying the missing word that explains why Khidr damaged the vessel.
variants.title: Addition of 'Salihah' ('Every Sound Ship') in the Codex of Ubayy bin Ka'b (Q. 18:79)
variants.diff_summary: In Tafsir al-Tabari (transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas via Sa'id bin Jubayr) and in the prophetic hadith of Ubayy bin Ka'b in Sahih al-Bukhari 2728, the reading of Ubayy bin Ka'b ('في قراءة أُبيّ') and the codex of Ibn Mas'ud ('في حرف ابن مسعود') include the adjective 'صَالِحَةٍ' ('sound / undamaged') in Q. 18:79: 'وَكَانَ وَرَاءَهُمْ مَلِكٌ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ صَالِحَةٍ غَصْبًا' ('behind them was a king seizing every sound ship by force'). Without 'صَالِحَةٍ', the literal Uthmanic statement that the king seized 'every ship' creates a narrative tension with al-Khadir's statement that damaging the ship would prevent its seizure.
variants.variant_target_english: seizing every sound ship by force.

variants.uthmanic_full_english: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working on the sea, and I wanted to damage it, (because) behind them (there) was a king seizing every ship by force.
variants.variant_full_arabic: أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتۡ لِمَسَٰكِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ فَأَرَدتُّ أَنۡ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٞ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ صَالِحَةٍ غَصْبًا

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari argues that the clause 'I wanted to damage it' in the Uthmanic text sufficiently implies that the king only seized undamaged ships, rendering the explicit word 'salihah' ('sound') in the codices of Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud unnecessary.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both Ubayy bin Ka'b and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud—two of the four primary Quran teachers appointed by the Prophet—independently preserved the consonantal word 'salihah' in their codices, demonstrating that it circulated as part of the recited Quranic text among senior Companions.

variants.short_title: Ubayy's Codex Adds 'He Was a Disbeliever' in Q. 18:80
variants.plain_english_hook: Al-Tabari records that in the codex (harf) of Ubayy bin Ka'b, verse 18:80 explicitly read 'As for the young boy, he was a disbeliever, and his parents were believers,' absent from the Uthmanic Quran.
variants.title: Addition of 'Fa-Kana Kafiran' in the Codex (Harf) of Ubayy bin Ka'b (Q. 18:80)
variants.diff_summary: In Tafsir al-Tabari (via 'Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar from Qatadah) and Sahih al-Bukhari 4727 (where Ibn 'Abbas transmits the account of Moses and al-Khadir from Ubayy bin Ka'b), Q. 18:80 in the reading (harf) of Ubayy bin Ka'b explicitly contained the clause 'فَكَانَ كَافِرًا وَكَانَ' ('he was a disbeliever, and [his parents] were'): 'وَأَمَّا الغُلامُ فَكَانَ كافِرًا وَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ'. This reading directly supplied the theological premise that the boy was already a disbeliever, which is absent from the Uthmanic consonantal skeleton.

variants.short_title: Word-Order Shift in Ubayy's Codex at 24:25
variants.plain_english_hook: In the standard Quran, 24:25 reads 'God will pay them their just [al-haqqa] due'; Jarir bin Hazim saw in Ubayy bin Kab's Mushaf: 'God, the Truth [al-haqqu], will pay them their due'.
variants.title: Surah An-Nur 24:25 — 'Yuwaffihimu Allahu al-Haqqu Dinahum' in Ubayy bin Ka'b's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 24:25, the verse reads يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ الْحَقَّ ('God will pay them their just due in full'), where الْحَقَّ ('the just/true') follows دِينَهُمُ ('their due/reckoning') as an accusative adjective. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record an eyewitness report from Jarir bin Hazim stating: 'I read it in the Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b: يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ الْحَقُّ دِينَهُمْ (God, the Truth, will pay them their due in full),' placing الْحَقُّ directly after اللَّهُ as a divine attribute.

variants.short_title: 'Ask Permission' vs 'Seek Familiarity' in 24:27
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran writes tasta'nisu ('seek familiarity'), Ibn Masud's codex and Ubayy's reading had tasta'dhinu ('ask permission'), with Ibn Abbas calling the standard word a scribal error.
variants.title: Surah An-Nur 24:27 — 'Tasta'dhinu' (Ask Permission) vs Uthmanic 'Tasta'nisu'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 24:27, believers are told not to enter other houses 'until you seek familiarity/ascertain [تَسْتَأْنِسُوا] and greet its inhabitants' (rendered by Droge according to the legal sense 'until you ask permission'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf read 'until you greet its inhabitants and ask permission' (حَتَّىٰ تُسَلِّمُوا عَلَىٰ أَهْلِهَا وَتَسْتَأْذِنُوا), while Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Abbas read 'until you ask permission and greet' (حَتَّىٰ تَسْتَأْذِنُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا), with Ibn Abbas explicitly stating that Uthmanic 'tasta'nisu' was a mistake by the scribe (أخطأ الكاتب / وهم من الكاتب).

scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari records multiple independent chains (via Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu'bah, and Hushaym from Sa'id bin Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and al-A'mash) attesting that Ibn Mas'ud's codex, Ubayy bin Ka'b, and Ibn Abbas all read 'tasta'dhinu' (with dhal) rather than 'tasta'nisu' (with nun), and al-Tabari himself adopts Ibn Mas'ud's sequence ('greet and ask permission') as the intended meaning.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا ابن بشار، قال: ثنا محمد بن جعفر، قال: ثنا شعبة، عن أبي بشر، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، في هذه الآية ( حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا ) قال: أخطأ الكاتب، وكان ابن عباس يقرأ "حَتَّى تَسْتَأْذِنُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا" وكان يقرؤها على قراءة أُبيّ بن كعب. حدثنا القاسم، قال: ثنا الحسين، قال: ثني هشيم، قال: أخبرنا مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، قال: في مصحف ابن مسعود: "حَتَّى تُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا وَتَسْتَأْذِنُوا". قال: ثنا هشيم، قال: أخبرنا جعفر بن إياس، عن سعيد، عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: "يَأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّى تُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا وَتَسْتَأْذِنُوا" قال: وإنما تستأنسوا وَهْم من الكاتب.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us... from Sa'id bin Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse: {until you ask permission [tasta'nisu] and greet its inhabitants}, he said: 'The scribe made a mistake. And Ibn 'Abbas used to recite, "until you ask permission [tasta'dhinu] and greet." And he used to recite it according to the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b.' Al-Qasim narrated to us... from Ibrahim, who said: 'In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud [it is]: "until you greet its inhabitants and ask for permission."' He said: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Ja'far bin Iyas informed us, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: 'O you who believe! Do not enter houses other than your own houses until you greet its inhabitants and ask for permission.' He said: 'And "tasta'nisu" is merely an illusion (mistake) from the scribe.'
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في مصحف ابن مسعود: "حَتَّى تُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا وَتَسْتَأْذِنُوا"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud [it is]: "until you greet its inhabitants and ask for permission."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وروى معاذ بن سليمان ، عن جعفر بن إياس ، عن سعيد ، عن ابن عباس ، بمثله ، وزاد : وكان ابن عباس يقرأ : " حتى تستأذنوا وتسلموا " ، وكان يقرأ على قراءة أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه . وهذا غريب جدا عن ابن عباس . وقال هشيم أخبرنا مغيرة ، عن إبراهيم قال : في مصحف ابن مسعود : " حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا " . وهذا أيضا رواية عن ابن عباس ، وهو اختيار ابن جرير .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Mu'adh bin Sulayman narrated from Ja'far bin Iyas, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas similarly, and added: "And Ibn 'Abbas used to recite it: 'until you ask permission (Tasta'thinu) and greet,' and he used to recite according to the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him." This is very strange coming from Ibn 'Abbas. Hushaym said: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, who said: "In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud, it says: 'until you greet its inhabitants and ask permission'." This is also a narration from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في مصحف ابن مسعود : " حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud, it says: 'until you greet its inhabitants and ask permission'

variants.short_title: 'Lay Down Some of Their Clothes' in 24:60
variants.plain_english_hook: Surah 24:60 literally permits elderly women to 'lay down their clothes'; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's readings added 'some of' (min), clarifying that only the outer cloak is meant.
variants.title: Surah An-Nur 24:60 — Addition of 'Min' ('Some of Their Clothes') in Ibn Mas'ud
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 24:60, elderly women past childbearing are told there is no blame on them 'that they lay down their clothes' (أَنْ يَضَعْنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ). Because laying down all clothes is universally forbidden, jurists restricted 'their clothes' to the outer wrap (jilbab/rida') by appealing to the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud (recorded by Ibn Kathir via Sa'id bin Jubayr) and Ubayy bin Ka'b (recorded by al-Tabari via al-Sha'bi), which read 'that they lay down some of their clothes' (أَنْ يَضَعْنَ مِنْ ثِيَابِهِنَّ).

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical exegetes treat the partitive preposition 'min' (some of) in the readings of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy as an explanatory clarification of what is already implied by context in the Uthmanic text.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari (citing al-Sha'bi for Ubayy bin Ka'b) and Ibn Kathir (citing Sa'id bin Jubayr for Abdullah bin Mas'ud) invoke this non-Uthmanic preposition to qualify an otherwise unqualified legal permission in the Uthmanic rasm.

Al-Sha'bi said: 'For indeed Ubayy bin Ka'b recites: "that they lay down some of their clothes [min thiyabihinna]."'

variants.short_title: 33:6 — 'And He Is a Father to Them'
variants.plain_english_hook: After stating that the Prophet's wives are the believers' mothers, the codices of Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Abbas added the clause: 'and he is a father to them.'
variants.title: Addition of 'And He Is a Father to Them' (Wa-Huwa Abun Lahum) in 33:6
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 33:6, the Uthmanic text states that the Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves 'وَأَزۡوَٰجُهُۥٓ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡ' ('and his wives are their mothers'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Abbas recited this verse with the additional clause 'وَهُوَ أَبٌ لَهُمْ' ('and he is a father to them'), a reading that al-Hasan al-Basri explicitly calls 'the first recitation' (al-qirā'a al-ūlā).

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical jurists and exegetes harmonize this clause as an explanatory note affirming the Prophet's spiritual paternity in respect and reverence, or as an early reading superseded by Surah 33:40 ('Muhammad is not the father of any of your men').
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari preserves al-Hasan al-Basri's designation of this wording as 'the first recitation' (في القراءة الأولى), and Ibn Kathir notes that Shafi'i jurists debated whether it remains legally valid to call the Prophet 'father of the believers' based on Ubayy and Ibn Abbas's reading.

Al-Hasan said: And in the first recitation [it is]: (Closer to the believers than they are to themselves, and he is a father to them).

tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It has been reported from Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn 'Abbas that they used to recite it: "The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves, and his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them." Something similar was reported from Mu'awiyah, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Al-Hasan. This is one of the two views in the Madhhab of Ash-Shafi'i, as reported by Al-Baghawi and others.

variants.short_title: 43:58 — 'Are Our Gods Better, or Is This Man?'
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of the polytheists asking 'Are our gods better, or is he?' (referring to Jesus), Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud read 'or is this (man)?' (referring to Muhammad).
variants.title: Substitution of 'Or Is This (Man)?' (Am Hādhā) for 'Or Is He?' (Am Huwa) in 43:58
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 43:58, following the mention of Jesus in 43:57, the Uthmanic text quotes the Meccan polytheists asking 'ءَأَٰلِهَتُنَا خَيۡرٌ أَمۡ هُوَۚ' ('‘Are our gods better, or is he?’'). Al-Tabari records from Qatadah that in the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy bin Ka'b—and in Ibn Kathir from Qatadah as the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud—this verse read 'أَآلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هَذَا' ('‘Are our gods better, or is this (man)?’'), shifting the comparison from Jesus to Muhammad.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’
variants.variant_target_english: ‘Are our gods better, or is this (man)?’
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَقَالُوٓاْ ءَأَٰلِهَتُنَا خَيۡرٌ أَمۡ هُوَۚ مَا ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلَۢاۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمٌ خَصِمُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: and they say, ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’ They only cite him to you as a (matter of) dispute. Yes! They are a contentious people.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَقَالُوٓاْ أَآلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هَذَاۚ مَا ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلَۢاۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمٌ خَصِمُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: and they say, ‘Are our gods better, or is this (man)?’ They only cite him to you as a (matter of) dispute. Yes! They are a contentious people.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators explain that under the Uthmanic reading 'or is he,' the Quraysh compared their idols to Jesus (since Christians worshipped him), whereas 'or is this' in Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud's reading was viewed as an interpretive gloss referring either to Muhammad or demonstratively to Jesus.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir, Qatadah explicitly cites the variant demonstrative pronoun 'أَمْ هَذَا' ('or is this?') and adds that the speakers meant Muhammad rather than Jesus.

variants.short_title: The Lost Verse of the Two Valleys of Gold
variants.plain_english_hook: Ubayy bin Ka'b, Ibn Abbas, and Anas bin Malik testified in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim that the 'Two Valleys of Gold' passage was recited as Quranic revelation before being omitted from the Mushaf.
variants.title: The Son of Adam and Two Valleys of Gold Passage Attested by Ubayy bin Ka'b
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari (6437, 6438, 6440) and Sahih Muslim (1048b, 1049), Ubayy bin Ka'b, Ibn Abbas, Anas bin Malik, and Ibn Az-Zubair report the prophetic recitation: 'If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would desire a second, and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust, and Allah turns in mercy to whoever repents.' Ubayy bin Ka'b states that the Companions considered this passage part of the Quran until Surah At-Takathur (102:1) was revealed, while Ibn Abbas and Anas bin Malik express uncertainty over whether it was revealed as Quran or prophetic speech.
variants.variant_target_arabic: لَوْ أَنَّ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَادِيَانِ، وَلَنْ يَمْلَأَ فَاهُ إِلَّا التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ
variants.variant_target_english: If the son of Adam had a valley full of gold, he would love to have two valleys, and nothing fills his mouth except dust, and Allah forgives whoever repents to Him.
variants.variant_full_arabic: لَوْ أَنَّ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَادِيَانِ، وَلَنْ يَمْلَأَ فَاهُ إِلَّا التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ
variants.variant_full_english: If the son of Adam had a valley full of gold, he would love to have two valleys, and nothing fills his mouth except dust, and Allah forgives whoever repents to Him.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators such as Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari explain that this passage was either an abrogated Quranic verse whose recitation was lifted after Surah At-Takathur (102:1) was revealed, or a Hadith Qudsi that some Companions initially mistook for Quran.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6437 and Sahih Muslim 1048b, senior authorities such as Ibn Abbas and Anas bin Malik explicitly state, 'I do not know whether it is from the Quran or not,' while Ubayy bin Ka'b and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (Muslim 1050) affirm that it was recited as part of a Quranic surah.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدٌ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَخْلَدٌ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَطَاءً، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لَوْ أَنَّ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ مِثْلَ وَادٍ مَالاً لأَحَبَّ أَنَّ لَهُ إِلَيْهِ مِثْلَهُ، وَلاَ يَمْلأُ عَيْنَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ ابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "If the son of Adam had money equal to a valley, then he will wish for another similar to it, for nothing can satisfy the eye of Adam's son except dust. And Allah forgives him who repents to Him." Ibn `Abbas said: I do not know whether this saying was quoted from the Qur'an or not. `Ata' said, "I heard Ibn Az-Zubair saying this narration while he was on the pulpit
hadiths.highlight_arabic: قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ
hadiths.highlight_english: Ibn `Abbas said: I do not know whether this saying was quoted from the Qur'an or not.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَقَالَ لَنَا أَبُو الْوَلِيدِ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، عَنْ أُبَىٍّ، قَالَ كُنَّا نَرَى هَذَا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ حَتَّى نَزَلَتْ ‏{‏أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ‏}‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Ubayy said (referring to the hadith above), "We considered this as a saying from the Qur'an till the Surah (beginning with):"The mutual rivalry (for piling up of worldly things) diverts you' (102:1) was revealed"
hadiths.highlight_arabic: عَنْ أُبَىٍّ، قَالَ كُنَّا نَرَى هَذَا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ حَتَّى نَزَلَتْ ‏{‏أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ‏}
hadiths.highlight_english: We considered this as a saying from the Qur'an till the Surah (beginning with):"The mutual rivalry (for piling up of worldly things) diverts you' (102:1) was revealed

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ يَحْيَى، وَسَعِيدُ بْنُ مَنْصُورٍ، وَقُتَيْبَةُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، قَالَ يَحْيَى أَخْبَرَنَا وَقَالَ الآخَرَانِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَوَانَةَ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لَوْ كَانَ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيَانِ مِنْ مَالٍ لاَبْتَغَى وَادِيًا ثَالِثًا وَلاَ يَمْلأُ جَوْفَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَحَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، وَابْنُ، بَشَّارٍ قَالَ ابْنُ الْمُثَنَّى حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا شُعْبَةُ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ قَتَادَةَ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ - فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَشَىْءٌ أُنْزِلَ أَمْ شَىْءٌ كَانَ يَقُولُهُ - بِمِثْلِ حَدِيثِ أَبِي عَوَانَةَ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Anas reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: 'If the son of Adam were to possess two valleys of riches, he would long for the third one. And the stomach of the son of Adam is not filled but with dust. And Allah returns to him who repents.' And Anas b. Malik reported: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying this — and I do not know whether it was something revealed or something he used to say — similar to the hadith of Abu 'Awanah.
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَشَىْءٌ أُنْزِلَ أَمْ شَىْءٌ كَانَ يَقُولُهُ
hadiths.highlight_english: I do not know whether it was something revealed or something he used to say

hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنِي زُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، وَهَارُونُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَطَاءً، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لَوْ أَنَّ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ مِلْءَ وَادٍ مَالاً لأَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ إِلَيْهِ مِثْلُهُ وَلاَ يَمْلأُ نَفْسَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ وَاللَّهُ يَتُوبُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَمِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ ‏.‏ وَفِي رِوَايَةِ زُهَيْرٍ قَالَ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَمِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ‏.‏ لَمْ يَذْكُرِ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Ibn Abbas reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:If there were for the son of Adam a valley full of riches, he would long to possess another one like it. and Ibn Adam does not feel satiated but with dust. And Allah returns to him who returns (to Him). Ibn Abbas said: I do not know whether it is from the Qur'an or not; and in the narration transmitted by Zuhair it was said: I do not know whether it is from the Qur'an, and he made no mention of Ibn Abbas
hadiths.highlight_arabic: قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَمِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ
hadiths.highlight_english: Ibn Abbas said: I do not know whether it is from the Qur'an or not

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا محمد بن خلف العسقلاني، قال: ثنا آدم، قال: ثنا حماد بن سلمة، عن ثابت البناني، عن أنس بن مالك، عن أُبيّ بن كعب، قال: كنا نرى أن هذا الحديث من القرآن: " لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مال، لتمنى واديا ثالثا، ولا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلا التراب، ثم يتوب الله على من تاب " حتى نـزلت هذه السورة: ( أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ ) إلى آخرها.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Muhammad bin Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to us, from Adam, from Hammad bin Salamah, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas bin Malik, from Ubayy bin Ka'b, who said: "We used to think that this statement was from the Qur'an: 'If the Son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would desire a third valley; and nothing fills the belly of the Son of Adam except dust, then Allah turns in forgiveness to whomever repents,' until this Surah was revealed: {Rivalry diverts you,} to its end."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: كنا نرى أن هذا الحديث من القرآن: " لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مال، لتمنى واديا ثالثا
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: We used to think that this statement was from the Qur'an: 'If the Son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would desire a third valley

variants.variant_arabic: لَوْ أَنَّ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَادِيَانِ، وَلَنْ يَمْلَأَ فَاهُ إِلَّا التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ
variants.variant_english: If the son of Adam had a valley full of gold, he would love to have two valleys, and nothing fills his mouth except dust, and Allah forgives whoever repents to Him.
variants.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدٌ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَخْلَدٌ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عَطَاءً، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لَوْ أَنَّ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ مِثْلَ وَادٍ مَالاً لأَحَبَّ أَنَّ لَهُ إِلَيْهِ مِثْلَهُ، وَلاَ يَمْلأُ عَيْنَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ، وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ ابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ‏.‏
variants.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "If the son of Adam had money equal to a valley, then he will wish for another similar to it, for nothing can satisfy the eye of Adam's son except dust. And Allah forgives him who repents to Him." Ibn `Abbas said: I do not know whether this saying was quoted from the Qur'an or not. `Ata' said, "I heard Ibn Az-Zubair saying this narration while he was on the pulpit
